text:
Tom Wilson ended a 16-game goal drought last weekend, a few nights after dropping the gloves off the opening faceoff, and that pretty much captures his season so far: all the usual edge, not much finish.

He has 3 goals on 5.95 expected through 21 games, shooting 8.3% when his talent range sits closer to 15%. This is a 30-goal scorer last season, and the chances are still there. Washington takes 53% of the expected goals with him on the ice at 5-on-5. Evolving-Hockey had him in the 99th percentile at taking chances away last year and noted his results already trailed his chances then.

The part to watch is the last ten games, where his ice time fell by almost two minutes and the Capitals created fewer chances with him out there than our numbers expected. That's either a slump in his game or a sign of shuffled lines. The finishing should come back. Whether the role does is the bigger question.
